claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys is governed by competition between configurational entropy and enthalpy of mixing.
The balance between configurational entropy and mixing enthalpy determines whether a single-phase solid solution or a multiphase microstructure forms.
Annealing at 1000–1200°C for 10–100 hours permits equilibrium phase formation.
Differences in atomic size and electronic structure among Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni cause lattice distortion.
Configurational entropy favors formation of a single-phase solid solution.
Enthalpy of mixing can drive phase separation or precipitation.
Lattice distortion mediates the entropy–enthalpy competition by changing the alloy energy landscape.
More compositionally balanced alloys have higher configurational entropy.
Alloys with higher configurational entropy have greater phase stability.
Alloys with higher configurational entropy retain a single-phase solid solution after annealing.
More compositionally biased alloys have lower configurational entropy.
Alloys with lower configurational entropy undergo phase separation or precipitation.
Phase separation or precipitation reduces high-temperature strength.
Phase separation or precipitation reduces environmental resistance.
Phase separation or precipitation reduces radiation tolerance.
Phase separation or precipitation reduces cryogenic toughness.
The hypothesis applies only to compositions within the single-phase solid-solution region of the phase diagram.
Observation of phase separation or precipitation in the tested alloy having the highest configurational entropy would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary restricts the hypothesis to compositions already within the single-phase solid-solution region, while the predicted comparison includes compositions expected to phase-separate or precipitate. Those outcomes would place them outside the stated scope.

The mechanism says phase selection is determined by competition between entropy and enthalpy, so even the highest-entropy tested alloy could separate if its enthalpic driving force dominates. The falsification rule instead treats phase separation in that alloy as decisive evidence against the competition mechanism.
The baseline Al0.1Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.3 is described as compositionally balanced, although its elemental fractions range from 0.1 to 0.3 and no quantitative definition of balance is supplied.
